Questions:

questions: Which existing methods are closest to training-time, context-subgraph-enriched supervision for multi-hop KGQA — subgraph retrieval/knowledge-augmented pretraining/graph-neural KGQA — and how much do they overlap?

Does the idea already exist under other terminology (subgraph-aware or neighborhood-aware KG embedding training, knowledge-graph-augmented LLM pretraining, contextualized fact supervision, query subgraph retrieval, intermediate/path supervision)?

Is the mechanism feasible: do standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks (MetaQA, WebQSP, CWQ, HotpotQA) provide source-passage provenance linking triples to a shared passage, and if not, which text-grounded KGs do?
What is the correct baseline and evaluation methodology (datasets, KG versions, splits, Hits@1 vs EM/F1, hop-depth transfer protocol) that a controlled comparison must follow?
Does any accuracy gain from context enrichment survive matched controls for number of examples, supervision tokens, and template?
Does an adaptive one-hop-failure repair loop genuinely reduce base-fact errors, or does it amplify label noise / reward-hack the failure detector?
Does RL-based optimization on lower-hop instances transfer to deeper-hop queries, or overfit shallow path patterns?

knowledge-graph-augmented language model pretraining and injection (ERNIE, K-BERT, KnowBert, KEPLER, KG-BERT, continual pretraining vs GraphRAG)
subgraph retrieval-augmented generation over KGs (DrKGC, GRAG, GNN-RAG, SG-RAG, Think-on-Graph, ToG-2)
query-subgraph / path-based multi-hop KGQA (EmbedKGQA, NSM/intermediate supervision, UniKGQA, QAGNN)
rejection sampling / self-training / iterative self-refinement / error-driven data augmentation (Self-Refine, STaR)
reinforcement learning for KGQA and multi-hop reasoning (DeepPath, MINERVA reward shaping, KG-Hopper, KG-Reasoner, GRPO-style objectives)
hop-length generalization / transfer in multi-hop reasoning and chain-of-thought
noise and incompleteness in knowledge graphs and robustness of KGQA to incorrect base facts
text-grounded knowledge graphs with passage provenance (HotpotQA supporting paragraphs, text-derived/temporal KGs)

NSM / intermediate supervision (He et al. 2021) - path supervision for KGQA
GNN-RAG (Mavromatis & Karypis 2025) - graph-neural retrieval for LLM KG reasoning
DrKGC (Xiao et al. 2025) - dynamic subgraph retrieval-augmented LLM for KG completion
GRAG (Hu et al. 2025) - graph retrieval-augmented generation
SG-RAG MOT (Saleh et al. 2025) - subgraph retrieval with merging/ordering of triplets

KagNet (Feng et al. 2020) - knowledge-aware QA over paths
KG-augmented LM pretraining baselines (ERNIE, K-BERT, KnowBert, KEPLER)
isolated-triple fine-tuning baseline (plain triple serialization, no context)

input.question: What is the correct evaluation protocol for 'transfer to deeper multi-hop queries' — is there an established held-out-hop split (e.g. train 1-2 hop, test 3 hop) on MetaQA/WebQSP/CWQ, or must a new hop-controlled split be constructed, and does the field report it?
input.description: MetaQA is naturally stratified by hop count (1/2/3-hop), which suggests a natural transfer protocol; WebQSP/CWQ are ~2-hop. Whether prior work reports train-on-shallow/test-on-deep transfer determines if the central claim is comparable to existing numbers or needs a bespoke setup.
input.rationale: If no established hop-transfer protocol exists, the headline finding has no baseline to compare against and the evaluation must be designed from scratch, changing the contribution substantially.

input.question: Are one-hop failures actually diagnostic of incorrect base facts, or does error propagate from composition/retrieval failures that a corrective-example loop cannot fix?
input.description: The repair loop assumes a one-hop failure localizes a bad base triple. If most one-hop errors come from entity linking, relation ambiguity, or question parsing rather than false triples, the repair signal is mis-specified and the loop may generate harmful corrective examples.
input.rationale: This determines whether the repair-loop component is well-founded or a built-in failure mode, and it is a prerequisite for any claim about 'reliability of base facts'.

input.question: How much does training-time context-subgraph supervision overlap with knowledge-graph-augmented LM pretraining (ERNIE, K-BERT, KnowBert, KEPLER) and with neighborhood-aggregation KG embeddings (R-GCN/CompGCN), which already train on entity neighborhoods rather than isolated triples?
input.description: The idea's premise is that training 'typically uses isolated triples'. GNN-based KG embeddings and KG-augmented LMs already condition on neighborhoods or entity descriptions at training time, so the premise may be overstated and the claimed gap smaller than assumed.
input.rationale: If established methods already train with context beyond isolated triples, the contribution narrows to the specific passage-provenance framing, which materially changes the novelty claim.

input.question: Is the three-component pipeline (context-enriched supervision + adaptive repair + lower-hop RL) too confounded to support a clean claim, such that the investigation should scope down to a single testable component?
input.description: Each component is a separate intervention with its own failure modes; running all three jointly makes it impossible to attribute gains and multiplies the chance of a null result. The likely refinement is to first establish the context-enrichment effect alone under matched controls, then add repair, then RL.
input.rationale: Scoping decisions at this point determine whether the contribution is a clean, attributable result or an uninterpretable bundle.

I added four new uncertainties to the three from the previous step — U004 (evaluation: is there an established held-out-hop transfer protocol?), U005 (validity: are one-hop failures diagnostic of bad base facts?), U006 (overlap: KG-augmented LM pretraining and GNN neighborhood aggregation already train on context), and U007 (direction: whether to scope down the three-component pipeline) — giving five open high/medium-importance questions plus the earlier feasibility and novelty ones.
